• From the Betta splendens complex. IUCN Red List: Least Concern.
  • Maximum size: 2.3 inches (about 6 cm).
  • Temperature: 75-85°F (24-29°C); much better coloration at warmer temperatures above 78°F (about 26°C).
  • pH: 5.0-7.0.
  • TDS: 60-200.
  • Breeding: bubblenester.

These fish are caught from the province of Hau Giang. Wild caught Betta imbellis from Vietnam. They are not line-bred and do not contain any hybridization like most Imbellis you have seen from farms, although they might contain some hybridization from the historical release of fighter-type splendens.

Only healthy, high-quality fish are selected for shipping; old fish or fish with any signs of disease or weakness are not sold. All fish go through 2 or more weeks of quarantine before being sold, including medication to remove parasites such as velvet and ich. All males come from the same lineage and are generally similar.

Be sure to have the habitat ready before purchase.

Native to Southeast Asia, including southern Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, and northern Sumatra, with introduced populations in Singapore. The fish offered here are caught in Hau Giang province, Vietnam.

Inhabits slow-moving, shallow waters: rice paddies, swamps, roadside ditches, and ponds with dense aquatic vegetation and leaf litter. Thrives in warm, slightly acidic to neutral water (pH 4-7), often with low dissolved oxygen, relying on its labyrinth organ for breathing.

• TDS: 60-200. They are kept in soft water with low TDS to match other wild bettas, but are more tolerant of water conditions.
  • pH: 5.0-7.0
  • Temperature: 75-85°F (24-29°C); much better coloration at warmer temperatures above 78°F (about 26°C).
Carnivorous. Currently fed live blackworms, frozen bloodworms and pellets.
Males are VERY aggressive and should be kept alone or in tanks with non-male betta mates. Can be kept in a planted community tank of multiple females if there is adequate space.

Body shape: Slender and elongated, characteristic of wild Betta species in the Betta splendens complex, reaching a maximum standard length of approximately 2.4 inches (6 cm). The body is slightly compressed, giving it a streamlined appearance suited for navigating dense vegetation.

Tail shape: Caudal fin is rounded or crescent-shaped, often displaying a distinctive red, crescent-like distal band, which inspires the common name "Crescent Betta." Fins are shorter and less ornate than those of Betta splendens.

Coloration: Base color is dark brown to black, overlaid with iridescent blue or green scales. Males exhibit vivid red accents on the caudal, ventral, and anal fins, with more intense coloration during courtship or aggression. Females are less vibrant, typically brownish with muted red or blue tints and faint iridescence. Like all wild fish, they have "green" metallic coloration with blue iridescence.

Operculum: Males feature striking iridescent blue or green scales on the gill covers, often with two vertical blue-green bars (occasionally red in some populations). Females have subdued opercular markings with minimal iridescence.
